text: Which perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) focuses on culture, organizational structure, leadership, and workforce skills?
explanation: The People perspective covers culture, organization design, leadership and cloud skills. The Governance perspective covers program management, risk and cloud financial management rather than workforce and culture.

text: A company must leave its data center before the lease ends in three months. It wants to move its application servers to Amazon EC2 instances as quickly as possible, without changing the applications. Which migration strategy should it use?
explanation: Rehost (lift and shift) moves applications to AWS without changes and is one of the fastest strategies. Refactor redesigns the application with cloud-native features, which takes much longer.

text: A company runs hundreds of virtual machines on VMware vSphere in its data center. It wants to move them to a VMware environment running on AWS without buying hardware, rewriting applications, or changing how it operates them. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Relocate moves servers from an on-premises platform to the cloud version of the same platform without new hardware or application changes. Rehost moves each application onto Amazon EC2 instances instead of keeping the same virtualization platform.

text: A company decides to stop running its own customer relationship management (CRM) servers and to subscribe to a software as a service (SaaS) CRM product instead. Which migration strategy does this describe?
explanation: Repurchase (drop and shop) replaces an application with a different product, commonly SaaS. Rehost and relocate move the existing application, and retain keeps it where it is.

text: Which of the following are perspectives of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)? (Choose two.)
explanation: The six AWS CAF perspectives are Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security and Operations. Sustainability, Reliability and Cost Optimization are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, not CAF perspectives.

text: During a large migration, a company sets up a secure multi-account landing zone, trains its teams, and migrates a small first set of applications to gain experience. Which migration phase is the company in?
explanation: In the mobilize phase, organizations build the foundation, including the landing zone, and migrate a small set of applications. The assess phase comes earlier and produces the readiness assessment and business case.

text: A company needs to lift and shift several hundred Windows and Linux servers to AWS. The servers must keep running during replication, and the cutover downtime must be only minutes. Which AWS service should the company use?

options.text: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with ongoing replication

explanation: AWS Transform MGN, formerly AWS Application Migration Service, continuously replicates whole source servers and allows a cutover with minimal downtime. DataSync copies files and objects, and DMS migrates databases, not entire servers.

text: Which statements about the AWS migration strategies (the 7 Rs) are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Repurchase means moving the same software unchanged to Amazon EC2
Retain means keeping an application in the source environment for now
Relocate requires the application code to be rewritten
Refactor is the most complex and costly migration strategy
Retire means moving an application to a managed AWS service

explanation: Retain keeps an application where it is, possibly to migrate later, and refactor is the most complex and costly strategy because it redesigns the application. Moving software unchanged is rehost, relocate needs no rewriting, and moving to a managed service is replatform.

text: A company wants to collect utilization data from its on-premises servers with an agentless collector and receive a data-driven business case that compares current costs with projected AWS costs. Which AWS service should the company use?
explanation: Migration Evaluator collects on-premises inventory and utilization data and produces a business case for migrating to AWS. Cost Explorer and Budgets analyze and forecast spending in AWS accounts; they do not assess on-premises servers.

text: Which activities belong to the assess phase of an AWS migration? (Choose two.)

options.text: Migrating applications at scale with a migration factory
Producing a high-level total cost of ownership (TCO) analysis
Building and securing the AWS landing zone
Modernizing applications after they run on AWS

explanation: The assess phase includes a Migration Readiness Assessment based on the CAF perspectives and a first TCO and business case. Building the landing zone belongs to mobilize, and migrating at scale and modernizing belong to the migrate and modernize phase.
